headline: High: Haystack’s MCP/REST outputs and broad egress can cascade into unsafe actions; prompt-injection and leakage are otherwise limited by the non-runnable awesome-cli-apps profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP servers and REST APIs, so it can ingest external content that may be attacker-controlled; awesome-cli-apps is a content-writing/list profile with no shared channel or parser details, so the pairwise bridge is inferred rather than documented. Uncertainty keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF Haystack is configured to consume content from an MCP server or REST endpoint that includes untrusted text, injection becomes plausible.
IF awesome-cli-apps is used as a source of instructions via copy-paste or file import, its content can be treated as authoritative by Haystack.
mitigations: Disable MCP endpoints not needed for the workflow.
Add a provenance tag to all external text before Haystack parses it.
Require a human review step before any instruction-like content is executed.
Restrict Haystack to allowlisted REST sources.
requires-engineering: add parser hardening and content-sanitization gates.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack touches anonymous usage statistics and has broad network egress, but no secrets or PHI are listed; awesome-cli-apps has no data classes touched and no shared workspace is documented. The plausible leakage path is limited and not evidenced as default, so low fits better than medium.
conditions: IF both agents are placed in the same shared workspace, file contents could be exposed across the pair.
IF Haystack is pointed at a source containing sensitive documents, its network egress can transmit them outward.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not route sensitive documents into Haystack.
Turn off unnecessary outbound connectors.
Use a local-only deployment for Haystack where possible.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack can call REST APIs and MCP servers, while awesome-cli-apps has no write or network surfaces beyond broad egress being listed; there is no documented shared mutable resource or locking conflict. The overlap is therefore limited and mostly hypothetical.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external API or MCP-backed resource, conflicting updates become possible.
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable directory, file conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials.
Avoid shared writable directories.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Disable MCP write tools unless required.
requires-engineering: add resource locking for shared backends.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG system that can consume upstream content and then surface it downstream; if awesome-cli-apps content is treated as authoritative, errors can propagate without verification. The pairwise pathway is inferred from Haystack’s role, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Haystack uses awesome-cli-apps content as retrieval input without a verification step, incorrect guidance can cascade.
IF Haystack is allowed to trigger downstream actions from retrieved text, the blast radius expands beyond a single answer.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before acting on retrieved content.
Mark retrieved text as untrusted by default.
Limit downstream actions to read-only outputs.
Require citations for any factual claim.
requires-engineering: add confidence-based gating before action execution.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent; Haystack only lists anonymous usage statistics, and awesome-cli-apps has no compliance-sensitive data classes. With no concrete mismatch, the compliance risk is limited to documentation gaps rather than a known breach.
conditions: IF Haystack is deployed in a jurisdiction with stricter residency rules and logs are retained externally, a policy mismatch could arise.
IF either agent is configured to process regulated data, the current documentation is insufficient to prove compliance.
mitigations: Review retention settings before deployment.
Avoid regulated data in this pair.
Document the data flow and hosting region.
Disable analytics if not needed.
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance attestations for the deployment.
